t: Section 458(a) of the HEA (20 U.S.C. 1087h(a)) is amended in paragraph (4) by striking “2016” and inserting “2017”.

fable.w: This section only makes a technical amendment to the Higher Education Act, replacing the year "2016" with "2017" in section 458(a)(4). It involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting opposite reading, since no outside party or decision-making process is mentioned at all.

opus.w: This section only changes a date in Section 458(a)(4) of the HEA, replacing "2016" with "2017". It creates no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties or right to sue. Being an amendment to a statute doesn't make it participation, because no outside party has any part in a federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** An amendment to the Higher Education Act (HEA) might look like it changes some agency process. It doesn't. The section only replaces one year ("2016") with another ("2017") in a provision about funding for administrative expenses. No one outside the federal government is consulted, invited to comment or given a hearing, an advisory role or a right to sue. Nothing in it involves participation at all.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific year from 2016 to 2017 in a referenced statute. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. It merely updates a date, which does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Section 458(a) of the HEA (20 U.S.C. 1087h(a)) is amended in paragraph (4) by striking “2016” and inserting “2017”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a date in a statute could implicitly affect participation timelines (e.g., for applications or reports), but the text itself contains no procedural requirements for public input, consultation, or coordination. It is a purely technical amendment to a deadline.
